content.text: An **inductive generalization** reasons from a sample to a whole population. It is only as good as its sample.

symbols.name: Big enough
symbols.meaning: More cases leave less room for chance.

symbols.name: Fairly chosen
symbols.meaning: Each member is equally likely to be picked.

symbols.name: Like the whole
symbols.meaning: Its groups match the population's groups.

content.definition: Choosing a sample in a way that makes some answers more likely.

examples.title: A good sample
lines: 1,000 voters chosen at random were asked.
examples.conclusion: So about 62% of all voters support it.

examples.title: Selection bias
lines: 75% of those who answer oppose the policy.
examples.conclusion: We cannot conclude that 75% of the public oppose it.
examples.note: Readers who answer chose themselves and may differ from everyone else.

question.prompt: A website poll shows 80% support for a candidate. Why might it mislead?
options: 80% is too high to be true
Its visitors chose to answer and may not represent all voters
Its sample is always too small
question.explanation: People who visit and choose to answer can differ from voters as a whole. That is selection bias.
